exposure: passive second stage of labor duration
cohort: The study included 460 nulliparous women at term who delivered under epidural anesthesia without pathological fetal heart rate and reached a second-stage passive phase of labor lasting at least 3 hours.
finding: Prolonging the passive second stage of labor to 4 hours did not increase maternal morbidity compared to 3 hours and resulted in a high rate of vaginal delivery (82%).
